summary:
Trends is the engine carrying this model right now — all four ratings show identical 14-day trends splits at 110-63 (64%, n=173), a full +7.5pts hot over season baseline, and SP is right behind it at 60% for R1/R2 (+7.4pts). That combo — trends + sp agreeing — has hit 57.2% on 458 decisions this season, and today's board hands you a loaded slate for it. R3 is the rating to lean on outright: 68% at 66-27 over the last 14 days for +33.0u, best of any rating, with strong-play ROI dwarfing the field at 56% season-long (+66.0u). R4, the newest rating, is right there too at 66% over its full 132-game sample with +25.0u — no fade signal yet, just consistency.

Today's board is stacked with clean consensus, and that's where the value sits. TBR at home over NYM is the standout: all four ratings agree with escalating conviction (R1 +2.89 up to R4 +3.44), and TBR as a liked team is money this season — 29-13 (69%) outright, 20-6 (77%, +22.0u) as a strong play. BOS over SEA is the second-best alignment (R1-R4 all between +1.11 and +1.37), and BOS as a picked team is the single best team angle in the data at 34-10 (77%, n=44) with strong plays running 18-5 for +17.0u — George Kirby on the mound only adds to it. TEX over ATH and MIN over DET both show full four-rating consensus with rising deltas into R4, worth trusting given R1/R2's hot SP form. On the fade side, don't overthink CHW/HOU, SFG/ATL, or MIA/WSN — all split decisions with sub-1.0 deltas, exactly the low-conviction spots where bullpen_fatigue keeps dragging every rating down to 42% over the last 14 days. Stick to the consensus games where trends and SP are pulling the same direction.
